top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a nameable phenomenon, the time-reversal-invariant Z2 insulator and quantum spin Hall state, predicted by Kane and Mele and decisively observed by Molenkamp in HgTe quantum wells, with nearly two decades of independent confirmation. The citation can be limited to the two-dimensional prediction and HgTe discovery, and the 2016 prize covered topological phase transitions and Chern-type phases, not this symmetry-protected class. The omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a real attribution gap but a limit of the three-name rule, not a defect in the discovery. P002 is a close second because its two-name credit is cleaner, but it overlaps more with the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes. P003 follows as mature but narrowly supported with a Crooks/Searles allocation problem, and no award is last because a sound, mature discovery is available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; TEM and oxide-interface work is only methodologically adjacent, and Goran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, but he supports P001 and has no tie to its laureates
